pr_title: Fix exception handling on DateFormatters.forPattern() with wrong date pattern
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/104124

Apparently there is a bug in `java.time` so that passing a wrong date pattern in some cases results in a `ClassCastException` instead of the expected `InvalidArgumentException` (see comment [here](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/104124#issuecomment-1921755275))

It's quite unlikely to catch this problem in a real production use case, but our randomized tests tripped over it.

The proposed solution is to also catch ClassCastException and in case wrap it in the expected InvalidArgumentException

comments: I cherry picked the mute to 8.12.

Interesting, apparently it's an old bug in OpenJDK
https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8193877

review_comments: Yes, it was intentional after Ryan's review. The problem is that randomizing the string does not guarantee that you'll get an invalid pattern, so it will make the test flaky. And producing random strings that are always invalid date patterns is not straight-forward
Shouldn't we randomise this? Or does the bug only manifest with some input format and this is such an instance? (We should add a comment if such.)
It happens only for some specific patterns, I linked the JDK bug as it explains the problem much better than how I could do it in a comment
Let's also check the cause, to make sure we actually got the ClassCastException we expected
👍 I'll add a check for that.
The ClassCastException which was caught by your change is added as the cause to the created IllegalArgumentException. We should be able to check the cause for that?

Yes sorry, I misinterpreted your first comment, I thought you meant to check that the CCE was actually due to the JDK bug, then I realized you just suggested one more assert in the test to check that the `IllegalArgumentException`'s root cause was a CCE.
I fixed it with my latest commit.
